authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 8857 prastara explicitly gives Prakrit patthara and regional pathar/pathara “stone”, including known cross-IA loans. Unaspirated patar remains a qualified phonetic variant within this identifiable stone family. Reviewed comparison: Rana pʌtʰʌɾa “stone” (f_dgvm3jmtklaei). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 9758 matsya explicitly gives Bshk. fish plural -cin and the eastern macharī -l/-r extension. Survey maśīn and macharī match those documented paradigmatic/extended forms, not the separate matsiya branch. Reviewed comparison: Rana mʌtʃʰʌli “fish” (f_v3htt7jh4gvf4). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 12598 śṛṇoti explicitly gives Bhojpuri sunal and western suṇṇo “hear”. Eastern -l and western -y inflections can continue the hear stem; sun-lo and ambiguous sunā causative/past forms require local morphology. Reviewed comparison: Buksa suna “he hears; he heard” (f_zzsmb6m2x457u). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.
